__
 
• **Eskers** are long, narrow winding ridges of alternately sorted material comprised of boulders and clay found in lowland areas. 
 
• They are formed by **fluvioglacial deposition**. 
 
• They are **ridges made of sands and gravels,** deposited by glacial meltwater flowing through tunnels within and underneath glaciers, or through meltwater channels on top of glaciers.
 
• **Esker formation presumably takes place after a glacier stagnates**, because the movement of the ice would likely spread the material and produce ground moraine.
 
• **Most eskers formed when glaciers were melting and retreating**.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about cell membranes.

options.text: Cell membranes are made up of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.
Cell membranes are made up of fats and fibre only.
Cell membranes are made up of lipids only.
Cell membranes are made up of roughage.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell membranes are made up of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane**, is a thin layer that surrounds the cytoplasm of all prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, including plant and animal cells.
 
• It is a **selectively permeable cell organelle**, allowing certain substances inside the cell while preventing others to pass through and thus is analogous to a barrier or gatekeeper in their function.
 
• It also serves as the** site of attachment for the cytoskeleton **that helps to provide shape and support to the cell.
 
• The main **components** that make up all cell membranes are **lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Their proportions of lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates vary between different types of eukaryotic cells, but their basic characteristics remain the same.
 
• For a typical human cell, **proteins account for about 50 percent **of the composition by mass, **lipids account for about 40 percent**, and the remaining **10 percent comes from carbohydrate molecules**
 
• . The arrangement of different proteins and lipids in the cell membrane looks like the arrangement found in a mosaic floor.

questions.question: Which is the only mangrove habitat in the world for the species Panthera Tigris?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sunderbans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sundarbans**, located on the delta of the **Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers in the Bay of Bengal,** is the largest contiguous **mangrove forest** in the world.
 
• The Sundarbans is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and represents an excellent example of ongoing ecological processes.
 
• It is known for its rich biodiversity, including **260 bird species, the Bengal tiger,** and other threatened species like the **estuarine crocodile** and the **Indian python.**
 
• The Sundarbans is home to the **Royal Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris**), which is the **only mangrove habitat in the world where this tiger species resides.**
 
• These tigers have uniquely adapted to living in the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans, making it a critical conservation area for their survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saranda Forest**__:

 __
 
• Located in **Jharkhand**, India.
 
• Dominated by** Sal trees**.
 
• Home to wildlife like elephants, tigers, and leopards.
 
• Faces ecological challenges due to iron ore mining.
 
 
 
• **Molai Forest**__:
 __
 
• In **Assam**, India.
 
• Created by environmental activist **Jadav Payeng**.
 
• Hosts Bengal tigers, rhinoceros, and other wildlife.
 
• A remarkable example of reforestation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Abujmarh Forest**__:
 
 
• In **Chhattisgarh**, India.
 
• Geographically isolated and inhabited by indigenous tribes.
 
• Alleged stronghold of Naxalite-Maoist insurgency.
 
• Known as “the **unknown hills**” in the Gondi language.

questions.question: To which of the following Gharanas did Hindustani Classical Vocalist, Bhimsen Joshi belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirana Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi **belonged to the **Kirana Gharana**, a prominent **school of Hindustani classical music**.
 
• The **Kirana Gharana **is known for its emphasis on intricate **melodic patterns**, **slow and meditative style**, and use of the** 'gayaki ang' **or **singing style**.
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi's** music was shaped by the **teachings of his guru, Sawai Gandharva**, who was also **associated** with the** Kirana Gharana**.
 
• **Joshi's** rendition of **classical ragas** and **devotional compositions** showcased the aesthetic of the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• His performances earned him **acclaim as one of the greatest vocalists in Indian classical music**.
 
• His legacy continues to **inspire aspiring musicians** and **enthusiasts** of **classical music worldwide**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra Gharana**

 
 
• Emerged in the city of **Agra, Uttar Pradesh**, in **medieval Northern India**.
 
• **Established** by **Haji Sujan Khan**, a **court musician** of **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan**.
 
• Has significantly impacted **Hindustani classical music**, **particularly vocal styles**.
 
• Includes **Faiyaz Khan**, **Vilayat Hussain Khan**, **Khadim Hussain Khan**, and **Sharafat Hussain Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Rampur Sahaswan Gharana**
 
 
• **Founded **in the princely state of **Rampur, Uttar Pradesh**, in the **19th century**.
 
• **Established** by **Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan** and **Ustad Mehboob Khan**, c**ourt musicians** of **Rampur**.
 
• Known for i**ntricate melodic patterns**, **rhythmic improvisations**, and **systematic presentation of ragas**.
 
• Includes **Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan**, **Ustad Nissar Hussain Khan**, and **Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior Gharana**
 
 
• Emerged in **Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India**.
 
• **Established **by **musicians patronized** by the **Scindia dynasty rulers**.
 
• Includes **Ustad Haddu Khan**, **Ustad Nathu Khan**, **Ustad Hassu Khan**, and **Pandit Vinayak Rao Patwardhan**.
 
• Profound impact on **Hindustani classical music,** particularly **vocal styles and compositions**.

questions.question: The famous source of Gupta empire, the Prayaga Prashasti is also known as the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad pillar inscription**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Samudra Gupta** court poet and minister **Harisena **composed the Allahabad pillar Inscription also known as Prayag Prasasti.
 
• The Pillar was an Ashokan Pillar erected by Asoka six centuries before him.
 
• This Inscription is a eulogy of Samudra Gupta and mentions the conquests of Samudra Gupta and the boundaries of the Gupta Empire.
 
• As per this inscription, Samudra Gupta defeated 9 kings in the North, and 12 Kings in the South, reducing all the Atavika states to vassalage.
 
• Allahabad Prasasti, composed by Harishena, does not bear any date and for this reason, historians have presumed that it was composed probably before the Ashwamedha Yajna performed by Samudragupta.
 
• They have opined this on the basis that there is no mention of the Ashwamedha Yajna completed by Samudragupta.
 
• The Allahabad Prasasti was originally engraved on the Ashokan Pillar in Kausambhi near Allahabad.
 
• Later it was moved to the Allahabad fort.

• The origin source of the **Sutlej **is west of the catchment area of **Lake Rakshastal **in **Tibet**, like springs in an ephemeral stream.
 
• **Ungti Chu and Pare Chu rivers** are tributaries of the Sutlej river.
 
• It finally **terminates **in the **Arabian Sea **near the port city of **Karachi, Pakistan**.
 
• **Bhakra Dam, Karcham Wangtoo Hydroelectric Plant**, and **Nathpa Jhakri Dam **are situated in the Sutlej River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As per the **Indus Water Treaty, 1960 **signed between India and Pakistan, the waters of three eastern rivers namely **the Sutlej, the Beas, and the Ravi **were allotted to India for exclusive use.
 
• **Bhakra Dam **is a concrete gravity dam across the **Sutlej River **and is near the border between Punjab and Himachal Pradesh in northern India. 
 
• Its reservoir, known as the “**Gobind Sagar**”, stores up to 9.34 billion cubic meters of water..

questions.question: Which of the following states used EVMs for the first time in the general elections held in May 1982?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First use of EVMs:** Occurred in the **general election** in **Kerala** in** May 1982**.
 
• **Absence of specific law:** Led to the **Supreme Court striking down the election**.
 
• **Amendment in 1989: **Parliament amended the **Representation of the People Act, 1951**, to **allow** for the **use of EVMs**.
 
• **General consensus in 1998:** Agreement reached for EVM introduction.
 
• **Initial usage in 1998:** EVMs used in **25 Legislative Assembly constituencies **across **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Delhi**.
 
• **State Assembly elections in May 2001:** EVMs used in all Assembly Constituencies in **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry, and West Bengal**.
 
• **2004 General Election: **Over** one million EVMs **used in all **543 Parliamentary Constituencies in India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India**

 
 
• Established on **January 25, 1950**.
 
• Mentioned in **Article 324** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• Comprises a **Chief Election Commissioner** (CEC) and **Election Commissioners**.
 
• Conducts elections to **Parliament, State Legislatures, and other offices**.
 
• **The president **appoints a **Chief Election Commissioner **and **Election Commissioners**.
 
• Tenure of **six years or until the age of 65**, whichever is earlier.
 
• They receive **salary, perks, and status equivalent to Supreme Court Judges.**

questions.question: Which year was designated by UNESCO as the International Year of the Periodic Table (IYPT) to mark the 150th anniversary of the Mendeleev Periodic Table?
questions.solution:

• The **International Year of the Periodic Table** (IYPT) was designated for the year **2019**.
 
• Designated by **UNESCO **to celebrate the **150th anniversary of the Mendeleev Periodic Table**.
 
• It **honoured Dmitri Mendeleev's** groundbreaking work on **organizing elements** into the **periodic table**.
 
• **Aimed** to raise **awareness of chemistry** and its **contributions to society**.

• **Mandate:** Promotes **peace and security **through collaboration in **education, science, culture, and communication**.
 
• **Objectives:** Focus on **education for all**, **scientific cooperation**, **cultural preservation**, **freedom of expression**, and **mutual understanding**.
 
• **Programs:** Includes **initiatives on education**, **World Heritage Sites**, **literacy, media literacy**, and **scientific research**.
 
• **Membership:** Consists of **193 Member States** and **11 Associate Members**.
 
• **Headquarters:** Located in **Paris, France**, with field offices worldwide.

• Spread the ideals of the **Brahmo Samaj**.

• Pioneering figure in **Indian socio-religious reform movements**.
